Washington, D. C. 20240
Dear Mr. Barber:
The State Planning and Development Clearinghouse has reviewed the following draft environmental impact statement prepared by the U.S. Department of Interior-Bureau of Sport Fisheries and Wildlife:
Proposed Endangered Species Conservation Act of 1972 SPDC Project No. 72-0949
During the course of our review, we have referred the environmental impact statement to the following agencies, which we have identified as interested in the environmental effects of the project or in developing or enforcing standards relating to these effects: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services; Board of Trustees of the Internal Improvement Trust Fund; Department of Community Affairs; Game and Fresh Water Fish Commission; Department of Legal Affairs; Department of Natural Resources; Department of Pollution Control; and the Environmental Information Center through which we received comments from the Florida Audubon Society, Archbold Expeditions of the American Museum of Natural History, and Mr. A. R. Marshall of the University of Miami.
Agencies were requested to review the statement and comment on the adequacy of treatment of environmental matters of their concern, additional alternatives which should be considered, and project modifications or special control measures to reduce or avoid adverse environmental effects. Agencies comments follow: The Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services; Board of Trustees of the Internal Improvement Trust Fund; Department of Legal Affairs; and the Department of Pollution Control offer no adverse comments on this statement. See attached letters. The Department of Natural Resources offers assistance in determining which species in Florida need to be placed on the endangered species list and in recommending procedures to insure protection of species on the endangered species list. See attached letter. The Department of Community Affairs offers no adverse comments by telephone. No response was received from the Game and Fresh Water Fish Commission. The Florida Audubon Society; Archbold Expeditions of the American Museum of Natural History; and Mr. A. R.
